description: Source-verified Museum paleodata. Only records with verification.status equal to source_verified are rendered by the app. Modern countries identify fossil collection locations, not reconstructed Mesozoic geography or a complete biological range.

verification.scope: Late Jurassic Archaeopteryx material from the Solnhofen–Eichstätt region of Bavaria; no Spanish Early Cretaceous occurrence is accepted here.

sources.citation: Rauhut et al. (2019), eLife 8:e43789
IUGS Geoheritage: Jurassic Solnhofen–Eichstätt Archaeopteryx serial site
Foth et al. (2025), Fossil Record: Archaeopteryx from the lower Tithonian Mörnsheim Formation

verification.scope: Brachiosaurus altithorax from the Morrison Formation of the western United States. Tanzanian material is excluded because it belongs to Giraffatitan.

sources.citation: Taylor (2009), Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 29:787–806
Taylor (2011), correction to the Brachiosaurus–Giraffatitan separation

verification.scope: Carnotaurus sastrei from the La Colonia Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina. A narrower numerical range is not asserted.

sources.citation: Bonaparte, Novas & Coria (1990), Contributions in Science 416:1–42
Gasparini et al. (2015), Cretaceous Research 54:154–168

verification.scope: Cryolophosaurus ellioti from the Hanson Formation of the central Transantarctic Mountains. No narrower numerical range is asserted.

sources.citation: Smith et al. (2007), USGS Open-File Report 2007-1047
Smith et al. (2007), Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society 151:377–421

verification.scope: Dilophosaurus wetherilli from the Kayenta Formation of northern Arizona. Historical Asian assignments are excluded.

sources.citation: Marsh & Rowe (2020), Journal of Paleontology 94(S78):1–103
Marsh & Rowe (2020), Dryad research dataset

verification.scope: Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis from Carnian strata of the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina.

sources.citation: Martínez & Alcober (2009), PLOS ONE 4:e4397
Martínez & Alcober (2010), ZooKeys 63:55–81

verification.scope: Confirmed Haplocanthosaurus material from the Morrison Formation of the western United States. Tentative records identified only as possible Haplocanthosaurus are excluded, and no narrower numerical range is asserted.

sources.citation: Foster & Wedel (2014), Volumina Jurassica 12(2):197–210
Curtice et al. (2024), The Anatomical Record

verification.scope: Majungasaurus crenatissimus from the Maastrichtian Maevarano Formation of northwestern Madagascar. Historical names now treated as synonyms are not presented as separate geographic occurrences.

sources.citation: Krause et al. (2007), Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 27(S2):1–20
Carrano (2007), Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 27(S2):163–179

verification.scope: Masiakasaurus knopfleri from the Maastrichtian Maevarano Formation of northwestern Madagascar. No distribution beyond this reviewed formation is asserted.

sources.citation: Sampson, Carrano & Forster (2001), Nature 409:504–506
Carrano, Loewen & Sertich (2011), Smithsonian Contributions to Paleobiology 95

verification.scope: Scutellosaurus lawleri from the Lower Jurassic Kayenta Formation of Arizona. Tentative cf. Scutellosaurus records are not used to broaden its published range.

sources.citation: Breeden et al. (2021), Royal Society Open Science 8:201676

verification.scope: Styracosaurus albertensis from the upper, late Campanian part of the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada. Broad stage-wide PBDB numerical bounds are not asserted.

sources.citation: Holmes et al. (2020), Cretaceous Research 107:104308
Brown, Holmes & Currie (2020), Vertebrate Anatomy Morphology Palaeontology 8:67–95
